title: Start a simple daily dua and dhikr
whyMatters: Dua and dhikr keep you connected to Allah long before you know much Arabic. They are small, portable ways to remember Him when you are stressed, when you are grateful, and in the middle of an ordinary day.

exactActions.text: Use your own words in dua
subSteps: Ask Allah for guidance, forgiveness, patience, and good people around you.
Speak in the language you understand best.
Keep it short enough that you will repeat it often.
Take the phrases from a teacher or a reliable guide so you learn them correctly.
Repeat them after prayer, while you are walking, or before you sleep.
Do not pile up long lists before you know what the words mean.

exactActions.text: Use a sound dua collection, carefully
subSteps: Choose collections that cite their Quran or hadith sources.
Learn what each one means before you add more.
If something has no source attached, check it before you pass it on.

obstacles.solution: You can make dua in your own language. Transliteration helps with short dhikr, but what carries it is knowing the meaning and meaning it.

obstacles.problem: I found a popular dua online
obstacles.solution: Do not assume every shared image or post is authentic. Stick to reliable collections, and ask a teacher when you cannot see where something came from.

tinyVersion: Once today, in your own words, ask Allah to guide you.
unlocksNext: Short remembrance holds up your prayer, your Quran reading, and your steadiness on the harder days.

commonQuestions.problem: Should I memorize a lot of duas right away?
commonQuestions.solution: No. Start with a few reliable duas or remembrances, understand them, and add slowly.
